runs.question: What fine does OMB M-25-21 set for an agency that misses its AI strategy deadline?

answer.text:
I could not find any fine in OMB M-25-21 for missing the AI strategy deadline. Across three searches of the memo, none of the passages mention monetary penalties, so I can't tell you an amount.

What the memo does set is the deadline and some consequences. For the strategy itself, within 180 days of the issuance of this memorandum, each CFO Act agency must develop an AI Strategy for identifying and removing barriers to their responsible use of AI and for achieving enterprise-wide improvements in the maturity of their applications. The strategy must also be made public. Agencies must use the AI Strategies template, to be provided by 0MB, and make their AI Strategies publicly available.

The memo does not state what happens if an agency misses that date. Its enforcement-type language covers AI use, not the strategy deadline. For example, if a particular high-impact use case is not compliant with the minimum practices then the agency must safely discontinue use of the AI functionality. Agencies also must continue with all relevant reporting requirements, including updating their annual AI use case inventory, compliance plans, and reporting as requested by 0MB.

If you need the consequences of a missed deadline, check the AI in Government Act of 2020 or any OMB follow-up guidance, since the memo's own text doesn't address it.
